_about: How the drone numbers in drone_table_2026-10-15.json were measured: machines, software, clocks, engines, protocols, caveats. The numbers themselves are rebuilt from raw/ by drone/make_drone_table.py.

policy.definition: GR00T N1.5-3B (nvidia/GR00T-N1.5-3B @ 869830fc, base model, frozen) vision-language backbone + a 1,348,672-weight drone action head trained by behaviour cloning on frozen GR00T features (drone/assets/drone_head.npz). No diffusion transformer.
policy.decision_path: raw 224 px FPV frame + 'fly to the <colour> pillar' + drone state -> GR00T's own input transforms (host CPU; frame resized to 256 first) -> SigLIP ViT (TensorRT fp16) -> pixel shuffle + mlp1 + embedding + image-token scatter (torch, NVIDIA deployment_scripts/trt_model_forward.eagle_tensorrt_forward, unmodified) -> Qwen LLM (TensorRT fp16, 296-token engine; the 289-token prompt right-padded with pad id 151643, mask 0) -> rows [:289] -> vlln + vl_self_attention (TensorRT fp16, 289-token engine) -> mean over 289 tokens (GPU fp32) -> head (numpy float64 on the host CPU, single-threaded BLAS) -> 16 x [vx, vy, vz, yaw_rate] setpoints, 20 ms apart
policy.engines: fp16, strongly typed, built by speed/build_engines.py: ViT and LLM = the 'A' engine build of the speed records (results/speed/groot_*_fulltrt_e2e_2026-10-12.json); vlln + vl_self_attention rebuilt at 289 tokens (it is bidirectional, so padding would change the valid rows) from the same ONNX

rtx5090.hardware: RTX 5090 32 GB, Intel i9-14900KF (8 P-cores = CPUs 0-15, 16 E-cores = CPUs 16-31), x86 Ubuntu
rtx5090.software: Python 3.12 venv: torch 2.9.0+cu128, TensorRT 11.2.1.2, numpy 2.5.2, MuJoCo 3.8.1 (= setup/requirements-x86-groot.txt + drone/requirements-drone.txt); contention workers in the system Python with TensorRT 10.16.1
rtx5090.clocks: not locked (default boost; nvidia-smi clocks recorded before and after every run in the raw files)

thor.hardware: Jetson AGX Thor developer kit (14 x Neoverse-V3AE), JetPack 7.2.1
thor.software: policy in nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.08-py3 (TensorRT 10.13.2.6, torch 2.8.0 nv25.08, numpy 1.26.4; setup/thor_container.sh); contention workers native with JetPack's TensorRT 10.16.2
thor.clocks: MAXN + jetson_clocks, read back before and after: CPU 2601 MHz, GPU 1575 MHz, EMC 4266 MHz

orin.hardware: Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB developer kit (12 x A78AE), JetPack 6 (L4T 36.4.7)
orin.clocks: MAXN + jetson_clocks, read back before and after: CPU 2201.6 MHz, GPU 1300.5 MHz, EMC 3199 MHz

machines.simulator_host_for_jetson_flights: the x86 machine above (CPU only): MuJoCo 3.8.1 with Mesa llvmpipe (LLVM 15.0.7) rendering, driving the board's policy server over an ssh tunnel; the network time is excluded from the delay

protocols.full_cost: 3 runs per machine, each a separate process: 64 decisions after 5 warm-up decisions, frame offsets 0 / 64 / 128 of the 256 gate frames. Each decision is timed from the raw frame to the setpoints (GPU synchronised at the start; the .cpu() copy of the pooled feature synchronises at the end). Rate = 1000 / median of the three run medians. The RTX 5090 was repeated with the process pinned to the P-cores and 8 torch threads, and as two 75 s loops (pinned, and unpinned with 24 threads).
protocols.output_gate: the 256 gate frames through the board's TensorRT path -> head -> the 4 setpoints a K = 4 loop flies, in vx / vz / yaw_rate, compared with the RTX 5090's eager bf16 policy on the same frames, in units of the training data's action standard deviation (sigma). G1 pooled RMS <= 0.07 sigma; G2 per-frame p95 <= 0.20; G3 a zero-image null must deviate >= 10 x G1; G4 a planted fault (another frame's features, same instruction) must fail G1. The thresholds were fixed before the first board ran.
protocols.closed_loop: 40 held-out episodes (seeds 7000-7039, colour = episode mod 4, start x and y uniform in +-4 m, 1.5-3 m up, random heading). Reached = within 0.8 m of the pillar horizontally, checked at every decision; budget 1,280 control ticks of 20 ms (25.6 s). Lockstep K: the simulator pauses for each decision, then flies K setpoints. Delay d: the drone keeps flying the previous chunk for d ticks after the observation (hovering before the first chunk lands), naive = the late chunk starts at setpoint 0, aligned = at setpoint d. Back-to-back: d = K = the decision's own latency rounded up to 20 ms ticks. All rendering with Mesa llvmpipe (bit-repeatable) except the 'nvidia' reproduction arms.
protocols.contention: the nav policy back to back on the 256 gate frames in one process; co-tenants in separate processes on the same GPU (default time slicing, no MPS). A nav decision counts in a window if it ENDS inside it; a co-tenant window is the worker's own [start, end] after its engine load and warm-up; solo = from 1 s after the nav is ready to the first co-tenant start; recovery = 1 s after a co-tenant ends to the next start (or + 5 s). Windows with fewer than 5 decisions are VOID. Every window's decisions are gated as above. 50 MP inspection burst = a segmentation stand-in over 190 tiles of 512 x 512 on zero inputs, 5 bursts 5 s apart; radar = a PointNet-style fusion stand-in at 20 Hz (or back to back); route planning = the segmentation stand-in at 1024 x 1024, one frame every 3 s (ASSUMED duty). Stand-ins: drone/contention/make_standins.py, seed 20261015, random weights.
protocols.contention_first_standin: the runs named *_c2_scan_0925standin used the first, unseeded stand-in of 2026-09-25 (same graph recipe, different random weights; not regenerable from this repo). The seeded stand-in matched it per tile on Thor (ratio 1.0007) and is 7% faster per tile on Orin (traced to the old default-init weights).

targets.why: any target from 23 to 39 Hz gives the same verdict (alone: the RTX 5090 and Thor meet it, Orin does not; during the inspection burst only the RTX 5090 does). We picked 30 Hz for this drone: it flies at about 2 m/s and takes a setpoint every 20 ms, so 30 decisions per second keeps each plan less than about 7 cm of flight old. In the simulator the reach numbers hardly depend on speed (it waits for the policy, or applies the delay exactly); on a real drone a slow brain flies on stale plans.
targets.range_note: 40 Hz would be marginal for Thor: its full-cost rate is 40.8 Hz, but its decisions while serving the closed loop took 25.5 ms (39.2 Hz) and one window of the all-jobs run measured 39.8 Hz.

caveats: Simulation only: a kinematic drone (velocity setpoints integrated every 20 ms, no aerodynamics), a toy scene with four coloured pillars, ~2 m/s, a 0.8 m goal. The flight controller that would track the setpoints is not modelled.
The policy is a frozen GR00T backbone plus a small behaviour-cloned head, not a GR00T fine-tune; a 3B vision-language-action model is far heavier than the navigation networks production drones fly.
The 50 MP inspection AI on the flight computer is a stress case: real drones usually run it on a payload computer or after the flight.
The stand-ins have random weights: their outputs mean nothing; only their compute shape and the gated nav decisions matter. Route planning duty is ASSUMED.
Reference = the RTX 5090's eager bf16 policy (what the head was trained on), not ground truth; bf16 is itself 0.023σ from fp32.
Closed loop: the simulator never runs while the policy computes; the delay arms apply the latency in simulator time instead. With 40 paired episodes only large reach differences are detectable.

RTX 5090 clocks were not locked, and its host CPU is hybrid: the full-cost decision takes about 7.2 ms with the Python thread on a P-core and about 8.6 ms on an E-core, and the OS moves it every few seconds. Short unpinned runs can land in either state; pinning (the pinned rows) removes it.
NVIDIA's full TensorRT path synchronises after every engine and uses no CUDA graphs; a fused export could be faster (not measured).
Predictions for every arm were written down before it ran; they are not reproduced here.
